question.text: Four forces F₁, F₂, F₃ and F₄ act at a single point O, as drawn in a force diagram. Write the x-component and the y-component of each of the four forces, measured along the ox and oy axes shown in the figure.
conditions: F₁ = 4 N, 30° above the horizontal ox line
F₂ = 4 N, 60° from the vertical dashed line, on the left side
F₃ = 6 N, directed straight down (negative oy)
F₄ = 4 N, directed along positive ox
all four forces act at the same point O

figure.description: Four force vectors are drawn from a common point O. A horizontal reference line runs through O; ox points to the right along it and oy points straight up. F₁ = 4 N points up and to the right, at 30° above the +x direction. F₂ = 4 N points up and to the left, at 60° above the −x direction (the 60° is measured from the leftward horizontal, so F₂ is 30° from the +y direction). F₄ = 4 N points horizontally to the right, along +x. F₃ = 6 N points straight down along −y.

solution.approach: Resolve each force along ox and oy using the angle it makes with the axes shown in the figure.

steps.text: F₁ = 4 N is at 30° above ox, so resolve it along ox and oy.
F₂ = 4 N is at 60° above the −ox direction (30° from oy), so its ox-component is negative and its oy-component is positive.
F₃ = 6 N points straight down along −oy, so it has no ox-component.
F₄ = 4 N points along +ox, so it has no oy-component.
Collect all four results as the final set of components.

common_mistakes.text: Measuring F₂'s 60° from oy instead of from the −ox direction, giving F₂ₓ = −4sin60° = −2√3 N and F₂ᵧ = 4cos60° = 2 N instead of the correct −2 N and 2√3 N.
Giving F₃ a positive oy-component instead of negative, missing that the arrow points downward.
